note: Hebrew 'elon is a large tree (oak or terebinth); the KJV regularly rendered it "plain" following some Jewish interpreters.

kjv: if the man should yet come thither
mine: Has the man come here yet?
note: The MT ha-ba 'od halom 'ish is awkward; read as a question "has the man come here?" (as the Septuagint understood it) it fits Yahweh's answer that Saul is already present and hiding, whereas the KJV's "should yet come" implies he had not arrived.
Hebrew yechi ha-melekh is literally "may the king live"; God is not named, and the KJV substitutes the English royal acclamation.
